extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys who represent clients before the USPTO; individuals subject to USPTO OED discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements governing attorney/practitioner conduct before the USPTO, the types of misconduct found (communication failures, neglect, unauthorized practice, failure to cooperate), and the sanctions/remedies imposed under USPTO rules and the Code of Professional Responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice / Unauthorized practice of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) (engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.505 (engaging in the unauthorized practice of law) by not withdrawing and continuing to represent clients in trademark applications before the Office when the practitioner was no longer qualified under 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.17(a) and 11.14 to represent trademark applicants due to administrative suspension of the practitioner's state law license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must not continue to represent trademark clients before the USPTO if they are not qualified under 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.17(a) and 11.14 (e.g., due to administrative suspension in the only jurisdiction of licensure). Failing to withdraw when unqualified can constitute prejudicial conduct and unauthorized practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) by allowing patent applications and trademark applications to become abandoned without the clients' knowledge and consent (examples: failing to respond to an Office action, failing to file a statement of use, failing to pay an issue fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must diligently prosecute client matters and respond to USPTO actions/requirements; abandonment due to practitioner inaction (not receiving/correcting notices, not responding to Office actions, not paying fees) constitutes neglect of entrusted legal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keeping the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) by failing to inform clients that their patent and/or trademark applications had become abandoned and failing to inform clients of important deadlines (e.g., issue fee deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must communicate timely and adequately with clients about the status of matters, deadlines, and options; failing to notify clients of abandonment or critical deadlines is a professional misconduct ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to maintain correct correspondence address and receive USPTO notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to maintain the correct correspondence address in a client's application led to not receiving a notice to file corrected application papers and consequent abandonment (fact pattern: incorrect correspondence address caused office notice to go undelivered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners are expected to maintain current and correct correspondence details for client matters so that USPTO mailings are received; failure to do so can result in lost notices and abandonment and may be misconduct-related when it harms clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counseling without full disclosure of material facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counseling a client against filing an appeal without explaining that the application was abandoned (fact: Respondent counseled Client No. 1 against filing an appeal, without explaining that the application was abandoned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When advising clients, practitioners must disclose material facts that affect the client's choices; withholding that an application is abandoned when advising against appeal is a breach of communication/ethical duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to cooperate in OED investigations / Timely response to lawful requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b) by failing to cooperate in an Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) investigation — specifically, not timely responding to a lawful request for information for six months without good cause (Respondent received an RFI allowing 30 days to respond but did not respond for six months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must timely respond to lawful RFIs from OED; the Final Order explicitly warns that 'a lengthy delay in responding to a lawful request for information from the Office of Enrollment without good cause may constitute misconduct.' Repeated reminders, certified mail returns, and voicemail attempts do not excuse prolonged nonresponse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification requirements to represent trademark applicants before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.17(a) and 11.14, practitioners must be qualified to represent clients in trademark matters; administrative suspension of a practitioner's state law license removes qualification to represent trademark applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must monitor their civil/licensure status in jurisdictions of licensure; if suspended or otherwise unqualified in the relevant jurisdiction(s), they must withdraw from trademark matters before the USPTO or otherwise cease representation until qualification is restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating effect of timely restitution and remorse
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'recognizes the seriousness of his misconduct,' is remorseful, and made timely or timely good faith efforts to make restitution to affected clients; the Final Order cites these as mitigating factors considered in determining discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making timely restitution to harmed clients and expressing remorse can be mitigating factors in disciplinary proceedings and may influence the OED Director's recommended sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary sanctions and imposed post-discipline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions imposed in this case include: six (6) month suspension from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters; remaining suspended until OED grants reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.60 upon reinstatement; publication of the Final Order in OED's e-FOIA Reading Room and a notice in the Official Gazette; dissociation of Respondent's name from Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; prohibition on applying for or obtaining a USPTO Customer Number (or being added to one) until reinstated; and each party bearing its own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary dispositions may include suspension, publication of the order, dissociation of electronic credentials, conditions for reinstatement, and restrictions on obtaining USPTO account access until reinstated. The Order also notes that the record may be considered in future proceedings as aggravation or rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and reliance on settlement agreements for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action resulted from a Proposed Settlement Agreement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 and statutory authority (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32). Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted at OED's e-FOIA Reading Room and a notice consistent with the Final Order is published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements under the cited statutes and regulations can resolve disciplinary matters and are publicly posted; practitioners should be aware disciplinary outcomes are publicly accessible and may be used in future disciplinary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order states that nothing prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) in: addressing further complaints of similar misconduct; as an aggravating factor in future discipline; to rebut statements by Respondent; and when considering any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary records remain part of the practitioner's history and can be used against or to inform future disciplinary actions, reinstatement petitions, or other administrative considerations.
